input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(ceq, TS_SUM(SUB(sstk, prstkc), 3)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book equity accumulated by recently selling shares is not evidence of cheapness; only book equity retained or repurchased against reflects real value, so removing three years of cumulative net equity issuance from the numerator sharpens the value signal.
input_signals.reasoning: This embeds financing directly inside the valuation ratio instead of adding a second sorting leg, mechanically penalizing serial issuers whose high B/M is an artifact of paid-in capital and rewarding repurchasers whose book has been depleted by cash returned to owners. The three-year window captures the persistence of financing policy while keeping coverage close to that of plain book-to-market.

input_signals.name: Cash flow yield times deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A high operating cash-flow yield is credible undervaluation when the firm is using that cash to retire debt; a low cash-flow yield combined with heavy new debt issuance signals a richly priced firm sustaining itself with borrowed capital.
input_signals.reasoning: This routes the financing channel through debt rather than equity, so it is a mechanically distinct source of information from buyback-based signals and avoids the option-grant noise in sstk. Net debt retirement is a costly, verifiable commitment that corroborates the cash-generating capacity implied by the valuation ratio, so the joint-extreme cells should carry the FF5 alpha.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Buyback value accretion per share
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The wealth transferred to continuing shareholders by a share transaction is the product of the fraction of the float transacted and the gap between fundamental value and price, so net repurchases executed at a deep discount to book accrete value per remaining share, while equity issued at a discount to book dilutes it and equity issued at a premium is largely neutral.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a rank blend of book-to-market and net payout: the two legs are multiplied because the accretion mechanism is literally a product, and the resulting cross-section is asymmetric in a way neither published anomaly produces — the most negative scores are cheap firms diluting shareholders (constrained issuers selling assets below book), not merely expensive issuers. Both legs share the same market-cap denominator so the product has clean units of book value acquired per dollar of market value, and the 1% symmetric winsorization keeps microcap firms with tiny market caps from dominating the tails.

input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( mul( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Repurchase timed to own valuation trough
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), TS_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Managers hold private information about their own firm's intrinsic value, so the informative event is buying back stock when the firm's valuation is depressed relative to its own five-year history, and issuing stock when its own valuation is at a multi-year peak; cross-sectional cheapness is not required for this timing signal to carry information.
input_signals.reasoning: The valuation leg is a within-firm time-series percentile rather than a cross-sectional value score, so this cannot be a re-labeling of book-to-market and avoids the sector- and business-model-driven level differences that make cross-sectional value traps, and it sidesteps the negative-enterprise-value denominator problem entirely. Both legs are bounded on [0,1] and the product is monotone increasing in each, concentrating longs in firms repurchasing heavily at their own valuation trough and shorts in firms issuing heavily at their own valuation peak — a pure managerial-timing interaction that neither leg identifies alone.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ts_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(revt, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dvt, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sales-to-price identifies firms whose revenue base is cheaply priced but says nothing about whether the cash is real; a contemporaneous increase in total dividends is a costly, sticky commitment that management makes only when it believes the depressed valuation understates sustainable cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: Dividends (dvt) have near-complete coverage back to the 1950s and dividend changes are far less mechanically correlated with book equity than buybacks are, so this leg should add information that HML cannot absorb, addressing the alpha-versus-slope divergence rather than restating it. Sales-to-price is chosen over book-to-market precisely because it is the value proxy least collinear with HML's book-based construction, and the change (rather than level) of dividend intensity keeps the signal from degenerating into a stale payer/non-payer dummy.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( revt, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( delta( ratio( dvt, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Both cheapness and buyback intensity are strongly sector-determined, so the informative comparison is within industry: a firm cheap relative to its own peers that is also retiring more equity than its peers is revealing firm-specific undervaluation rather than sector-level pricing.
input_signals.reasoning: The generation-0 buyback-value signals had solid FMB t-stats but zero FF5 alpha, consistent with the long-short spread being a sector value tilt that HML and CMA already price; industry-relative ranking on both legs strips exactly that component and leaves the idiosyncratic managerial-information component. input_signals.hypothesis: Buyback and issuance levels are highly persistent and therefore largely anticipated, so the surprise lies in the transition — a firm that swings from net issuer to net repurchaser while trading at a high earnings yield is delivering new information about management's view of its own price.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal used the level of the financing state; this isolates the change, which is the natural candidate for unpriced information and for a spread that FF5 factors (built from slow-moving level characteristics) cannot span. If the change-based version delivers alpha where the level-based versions did not, that identifies staleness — not sample or scaling — as the binding constraint on the whole family.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Discounted cash released by payout
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(che, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dvt, che), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The market applies a deep discount to cash it believes will be hoarded or wasted, so a firm whose cash balance is large relative to its market capitalization is mispriced only if management is actually releasing that cash to owners; the payout rate out of the cash stock is the catalyst that converts a balance-sheet discount into realized return.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the leverage/deleveraging channel entirely and prices a different asset — the cash stock itself — so it is not a variable substitution on the archived cash-flow-yield-times-deleveraging bet, and the agency mechanism (trapped cash discount released by distribution) is specific to the pairing rather than to either leg alone. Cash-to-price alone is a distress-tilted, HML-correlated value proxy and the payout rate out of cash alone is a maturity proxy, but their joint tail — cheap cash that is verifiably being distributed — is the agency-discount-closing cell, and both che and dvt are populated across essentially the full panel so the portfolios stay wide.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( che, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( dvt, che ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Payout instrument tilted to buybacks when cheap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Conditional on returning capital at all, the *choice* of instrument reveals management's price view: repurchases are the value-accretive instrument only when the stock is cheap, so a cheap firm that skews its payout mix toward buybacks rather than dividends is making a price-contingent capital allocation decision that a dividend-paying peer is not.
input_signals.reasoning: This holds total payout roughly fixed and varies only its composition, so unlike every archive signal it is not a payout-yield or net-issuance bet and should carry little RMW or HML loading — the mechanism is capital allocation skill conditional on price, not the amount of cash returned. The mix ratio is bounded in [−1,1] by construction, which keeps the rank well behaved, and the interaction is essential: a buyback-tilted mix at a high price is value destruction, so neither leg carries the hypothesis alone.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( prstkc, dvt ), add( prstkc, dvt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Raising equity while paying it back out
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), revt)), IND_RANK(MIN(RATIO(sstk, at), RATIO(dvt, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that simultaneously sells new shares and distributes cash to existing holders is round-tripping capital at a cost; when it does so from a rich price-to-sales multiple, the issuance is opportunistic use of overvalued currency and the dividend is a signaling expense, so subsequent returns should be low.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN operator identifies simultaneity — a state neither net external financing nor gross issuance can express, since netting these flows makes a raise-and-distribute firm look financially neutral — so this is not the XFIN anomaly relabeled, and it avoids gross dltis entirely and with it the revolver-rollover contamination. The financing leg is industry-ranked to prevent the signal from collapsing into a REIT and utility bet, where mandatory distribution plus continuous equity issuance is structural rather than informative, and the rich-multiple leg is on the short side where generation 1's negative sales-yield alpha says the price-multiple return actually lives.

input_signals.hypothesis: The instrument-choice signal reflects a standing capital-allocation policy rather than a single year's tender offer, so measuring the buyback-versus-dividend tilt over three years of cumulative payout captures the persistent managerial view of price while filtering out one-off transactions and years of accidental zero payout.
input_signals.reasoning: A three-year cumulation defines the mix for any firm that paid out at all in the window, which should lift coverage above the 0.079 of the single-year version and stabilize decile membership month to month — the two diagnostics most likely to be limiting the winner's alpha t-stat. It isolates a single design choice (measurement horizon of the composition variable) against the archive's best result, so the contrast is directly interpretable as noise-versus-signal in the mix leg.

input_signals.hypothesis: Payout instrument norms are set at the industry level — utilities and staples distribute through dividends by convention while technology and healthcare distribute through repurchases — so the price-contingent decision is a firm's deviation from its own sector's payout convention, not its position in the pooled cross-section.
input_signals.reasoning: The pooled mix rank almost certainly contains a large static sector component that adds noise to the interaction and drags the long leg toward whole industries; ranking the mix within industry strips that component and leaves the firm-specific instrument choice the hypothesis is about. input_signals.reasoning: This discriminates between two very different readings of the archive's best result: a pure composition effect (bounded ratio, payers only) versus a signed magnitude effect (unbounded intensity, whole cross-section). If the intensity version reproduces the alpha, the mechanism is robust and coverage nearly doubles; if it collapses, we learn that the information is specifically in the *choice conditional on paying out*, which sharpens every subsequent refinement.

input_signals.name: Equity versus debt retirement when cheap

input_signals.hypothesis: A firm with cash to return faces a relative-value decision between retiring its own equity and retiring its own debt; choosing equity while the stock trades at a high earnings yield reveals that management judges its equity to be the cheaper claim to repurchase, whereas paying down debt at the same price reveals the opposite.
input_signals.reasoning: This applies the instrument-choice logic that worked to an entirely different decision margin — across the capital structure rather than between two forms of shareholder payout — so it tests whether the mechanism is "management picks the mispriced claim" or narrowly "buybacks beat dividends." Both components are uses of cash rather than a use versus a source, so the ratio is bounded and interpretable, and the cell is disjoint from the dividend-mix cell, giving genuinely incremental evidence rather than a rescaling.

input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that distributes nothing has made no instrument choice and should be scored neutrally rather than dropped, so the payout-mix signal should extend to the full cross-section with non-payers placed between the dividend-only and buyback-only extremes.

The COALESCE convention is economically justified rather than a coverage patch: when total payout is zero the fallback evaluates to exactly zero, which is precisely the neutral midpoint of the [−1, 1] mix scale, so the ordering of genuine payers is untouched while non-choosers occupy the middle.
